# Review of the annotation of a five-sentence Chinese document (founding and circulation history of a tabloid)

Most checks are high. These cost the most: aspect (F 73), reentrancy (F 0), temporal (F 83), modal (P 75) and coreference (P 71). Almost every lost unit comes from one of the patterns below. They are listed from most to least costly.

## 1. Over-annotating the decomposed "verb + 量" quantity noun (about 12 units)
**Checks:** c_aspect (4 extra), i_modal (4 extra), h_temporal (2 extra), j_coref (2 extra).

**What happened:** The annotator split the quantity noun correctly into `量 :quant-of verb` plus `have-quant-91`. It then treated both inner nodes as full events:
- it gave the inner verb `:aspect process` and an author modal link;
- it gave `have-quant-91` `:aspect state`, a temporal parent and a modal parent.

The gold gives neither inner node an aspect. Neither gets a modal link, and `have-quant-91` gets no temporal link. Only the inner verb gets a temporal link: `:overlap` with the clause verb.

The annotator also linked the two quantity nouns of two sentences as `:same-entity`. They are the same measure at different dates with different values, and the gold links nothing.

**Why:** Three general rules pulled the annotator the wrong way, and there is no exception for this structure:
- aspect step 3 ("a process noun → process");
- "every node that carries :aspect gets a modal parent";
- "a process nominal … do not leave it without a parent".

**Change:** Add to the quantity-noun rule in 3.1 and 5.1:
- "In a decomposed quantity noun, neither the inner verb nor the `have-quant-91` gets `:aspect`.
- Neither gets a modal link.
- Only the inner verb gets a temporal link (`:overlap` with the clause verb). `have-quant-91` gets none.
- A measure noun (circulation, sales, population, price) mentioned again at another time, with another value, is not coreferent. Corefer only its owner entity."

## 2. Where a named work goes in a long sentence with several clauses, and its re-entrancy (about 5 units)
**Checks:** g_reentrancy (1 missing, 1 extra), d_peripheral_entity (1 extra, 1 missing), plus a placement that cost a core role.

**What happened:**
- The tabloid is the subject of a change clause ("X will change from A layout to B layout"). The annotator built the tabloid in full later, inside a "does not meet X's standard" clause, and pointed back with an inverse `:part` to the change clause's component noun.
- The gold builds the named entity, with its apposition, where it first appears in reading order: as `:part-of` of the component noun (the layout). It then uses a re-entrancy for the later `:possessor`.

**Why:** The instruction says nothing about which mention of a re-used entity carries the full node. It also does not say that the topic of a change clause is the whole, of which the changed component is a part.

**Change:**
- "When an entity occurs more than once in a sentence, write its full node (name, apposition) at its first occurrence in reading order. Later mentions are re-entrancies.
- In 'X 由 A 改为 B', when A and B are components (layout, edition, format) of the subject X, X is `:part-of` on A. X is not a separate argument, and the relation is not written as an inverse `:part`."

## 3. Attaching a trailing descriptive clause when the object is "component of a named work" (2 units)
**Checks:** d_core_args, c_aspect.

**What happened:**
- The object was "[colour] 版面 的 《N》", which the component rule correctly makes `版面 :part-of 《N》`. The annotator then attached the trailing clause "containing articles …" to the named work. The gold attaches it to the head component noun.
- The annotator gave the containing verb `state`; the gold gives `process`.

**Why:**
- The relative-clause rule says "attach to the object just introduced", but it does not say which node that is when the object has been restructured.
- The aspect rule says "the capacity or content of a publication … (`process` or `state`)". That leaves the choice open, and the annotator picked the wrong one.

**Change:**
- "When the object has been restructured by the component rule, a trailing relative clause attaches to the head node of the object, the component noun.
- A verb saying what a publication or its section contains or holds is `process`." Remove "or state".

## 4. Appositive `identity-91` inside a noun phrase gets attributes (2 units)
**Checks:** c_aspect (extra), i_modal (extra).

**What happened:** The annotator gave the apposition reification of the named tabloid `:aspect state` and an author modal link. The gold gives it neither.

**Why:** The instruction says "copular and identity predicates … do get a modal parent". It does not tell a predicated identity ("A is a B") apart from an appositive one.

**Change:** "An `identity-91` that reifies an apposition inside a noun phrase gets no `:aspect`, no temporal link and no modal link. Only a predicated identity (a copular sentence) gets a modal parent."

## 5. Linking a sentence to the previous one with "also" (1 unit, structural)
**Check:** h_temporal.

**What happened:** The sentence says the printing style "also became" the publication's feature. The annotator anchored its main event to `document-creation-time :before`. The gold uses `(previous anchor :overlap main event)`.

**Why:** The rule exists ("*also became* … 于是 → `:overlap`"), but the annotator did not follow it. The word "also" (也) is not listed as a trigger.

**Change:** List 也/还 + a change-of-state verb (成, 成为, 变成) explicitly among the triggers that link the anchor to the previous sentence's anchor with `:overlap`.

## 6. Habitual aspect for a production practice used as a noun subject (1 unit)
**Check:** c_aspect.

**What happened:** "Black-and-white printing became its feature." The annotator gave printing `process`, following step 3. The gold gives `habitual`.

**Why:** Step 1 is limited to "Only verbs of publishing or reporting", so printing was excluded.

**Change:** Widen step 1 to the routine production practices of a publication or organisation: printing, issuing, publishing, broadcasting. Say that step 1 also wins when the event is a noun used as an argument.

## 7. Decade dates (2 units, plus the decade's temporal relation)
**Checks:** c_other_attributes, h_temporal.

**What happened:**
- The annotator wrote `:decade 1980`, but the instruction already says "Decades (X年代) use `:era`". This is a rule not followed, so make it stand out: put it in the Dates paragraph and in the checklist.
- It used `:contained` because a decade is "a long span". The gold uses `:overlap`.

**Change:** "A date expression of the clause, whether a year, a decade or a span, takes its event with `:overlap`." Drop the `:contained` exception, or limit it to explicit "during/within" wording.

## 8. A frame for a connective that opens a sentence (1 unit)
**Check:** a_event_found.

**What happened:** The annotator built `but-91` with only `:ARG2` for a 不过 at the start of a sentence. The gold has no such node.

**Change:** "A connective at the start of a sentence (不过, 但是, 然而, 因此) that relates the sentence to an earlier one gets no discourse frame. Annotate the clause alone."

## Minor
- The gold uses a `-00` sense for the founder verb inside the "verb + 人" role noun, although PropBank has `-01`. This costs 1 unit and is likely a gold inconsistency. No change is needed.

## Keep these rules: the annotator applied them correctly
- The reified `have-reason-91` / `have-purpose-91` nesting, with `state` aspect and author links.
- `have-org-role-91` with the "人 + `:ARG0-of` verb" founder role noun.
- Named entities with the 《》 tokens and the `·` token, `newspaper` as the type, and no `:wiki`.
- The component noun as `:part-of` the work.
- The change frame with `:ARG1` / `:ARG2` (not `:source`).
- The split of the quantity noun with `have-quant-91` and the classifier as `:unit`.
- Temporal linking inside the sentence:
  - the purpose clause `:overlap`s its main event;
  - the event left over from earlier is `:before` the event of its clause;
  - the reason clause is ordered with `:before` against its result.
- `full-negative` for the negated "meet" verb.
- The `已经` and `也` adverbs as `:mod` on the predicate.
- Coreference of the publication across sentences, each mention linked to its closest earlier one.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
I made eight compact edits. Each targets a pattern from the critique that will recur on other documents, and the total stays under the 30,000-character limit.

1. **Decomposed quantity noun.** The inner verb and `have-quant-91` get no `:aspect` and no modal link, and `have-quant-91` gets no temporal link. The same measure at another time or with another value is not coreferent.
2. **Full node at first occurrence.** An entity used twice in a sentence is written in full at its first mention in reading order; later mentions are re-entrancies. In 由X改为Y with component nouns, the subject is `:part-of` on X.
3. **Trailing clause on a restructured object.** It attaches to the component noun. A verb saying what a publication contains is `process`, no longer "process or state".
4. **Appositive `identity-91`.** It gets no aspect and no temporal or modal links.
5. **Linking to the previous sentence.** 也/还 + a change-of-state verb is now listed as a trigger for this link.
6. **Habitual step.** It now covers routine production practices such as printing, including when the event is a noun used as an argument.
7. **Dates.** A decade is `:era`, never `:decade`. Years and decades take `:overlap`; `:contained` is kept only for explicit during/within wording.
8. **Sentence-initial connective.** It gets no discourse frame.

critique
Most checks were perfect: temporal, modal, coreference, polarity, named entities, event and entity concepts. All of the misses come from three kinds of construction. The costliest one is where the full node of a named entity goes when the entity is mentioned twice in one sentence.

## 1. A named entity mentioned twice in one sentence: full node at the wrong mention, wrong roles around it (most costly)
**Cost:** about 7 units.
- g_reentrancy dropped to 0: one re-entrancy missing, one extra.
- d_peripheral_entity: 3 units (an extra `:possessor`, a wrong `:mod`, a missing `:mod` on the apposition noun).
- The `:part`/`:part-of` edge was also counted wrong.

**What happened:** A periodical is named first as the owner of a component noun inside a change construction ("由 X 改为 Y", where X is a layout or edition of the periodical). It is named again later in the sentence as the possessor of a standard.
- The annotator wrote the full node (name, apposition, modifiers) at the later mention, because that comes first when you walk the graph.
- It then pointed back to the component with an inverse `:part`.
- The gold writes the full node at the first mention in the text, as `:part-of` on the component noun. The later possessor is a re-entrancy.

**Why it happened:**
- The instruction says "first occurrence in reading order", which can be read as graph order.
- The change-verb rule already says "not an inverse `:part`", but the annotator did not apply it. This is probably because the periodical was written somewhere else in the graph.
- A related slip: an attributive word in front of the apposition noun ("旗下的 [modifier] 小报 《N》") was attached to the named entity, not to the apposition noun it modifies in the text.

**Changes:**
- Say plainly: "Reading order" means the order of the words in the sentence, not the order of the PENMAN graph. When the same entity appears twice in one sentence, the full node (name, apposition, all its modifiers) goes at the word-first mention, even if that mention is lower in the graph. Every other mention is a bare variable.
- Repeat in the change-verb rule: the subject is `:part-of` on X even when it also fills a role elsewhere. Never add `:part` from the entity back to X.
- Add: modifiers written before an apposition noun (`的`-phrases, 旗下, property words) attach to the apposition noun inside `identity-91 :ARG2`, not to the named entity.

## 2. Role direction in `have-org-role-91` for a role noun before a name
**Cost:** 2 units (d_core_args_abstract partial, e_core_labels wrong).

**What happened:** The annotator wrote `:ARG0-of` where the instruction's own template says `:ARG1-of`. The rule was there and was not followed. Most likely the "role noun = verb + 人/者" pattern `:ARG0-of (v / verb…)` sat right next to it and its `:ARG0-of` leaked over.

**Change:** In 2.2 and in the checklist, add: "The holder of a title is always `:ARG1` of `have-org-role-91` (`:ARG1-of` on the person). `:ARG0` is never used with `have-org-role-91`/`have-rel-role-92`." Keep the `:ARG0-of` template for the inner verb of a verb + 人 role noun, and present it clearly as a separate case.

## 3. Aspect of a habitual practice named by a process nominal
**Cost:** 1 unit (c_aspect).

**What happened:** A process nominal named a way of producing a publication (printing in a certain manner) and was the subject of "became the publication's feature". The gold marks it `habitual`; the annotator used `process` (step 3).

**Why it happened:** Step 1 lists only "publishing, reporting, compiling, broadcasting". It also does not say that step 1 comes before step 3 for nominals.

**Change:** Widen step 1 to cover any production or distribution activity of a periodical or organisation (printing, issuing, distributing, broadcasting). Say it applies to process nominals too: a nominal naming the routine practice of an entity, especially as the subject of "is or became its feature or trademark", is `habitual`, not `process`.

## 4. Aspect of a relative-clause verb that says what a new publication will hold
**Cost:** 1 unit (c_aspect: gold `process`, annotator `state`).

**Why it happened:** Step 1 says the capacity or content of a publication is "`process` or `state`" and leaves the choice open.

**Change:** Settle it: a verb saying what a publication or container holds or carries (contains, holds, carries articles) is `process`. Keep `state` for plain possession, being and belonging verbs.

## 5. Sense of a verb morpheme split out of a role noun
**Cost:** 1 unit (b_event_sense).

**What happened:** For the inner verb of a verb + 人 role noun, the gold used `-00` even though a PropBank roleset (`-01`) exists for that verb.

**Change (low confidence, it rests on one case):** When the inner verb is split out of a verb + 人/者 role noun and is a bound morpheme, not used as a free verb in the sentence, use `<morpheme>-00`. Check the gold data with `search_annotations` before applying this widely.

## What to keep
The annotator followed these rules exactly, and they gave 100% on their checks:
- The reified `have-reason-91` / `have-purpose-91` nesting for a paired reason/result plus a marked purpose, with author links and no temporal parent.
- The "verb + 量" split with `have-quant-91` and its classifier unit, and no aspect on either.
- The temporal rules:
  - date `:overlap` on the event, and `:before` from `document-creation-time` to an absolute past date;
  - `:era` for a decade;
  - a past participle `:before` the event it modifies (the `(main :before rc-event)` rule);
  - a reason event `:before` its result;
  - a sentence with 也成 linked `:overlap` to the earlier event it continues from;
  - a process nominal `:overlap` with its verb.
- The modal rules: `full-negative` with `:polarity -`, and `author :full-affirmative` on every node that has an aspect.
- Coreference to the closest earlier mention.
- The title marks kept as name ops, the middle dot kept as its own op, no `:wiki`.
- A demonstrative + 刊 written as `刊 :mod 该`.
- The component noun as head with the work as `:part-of` (the 版 的 《N》 rule).
- Adverbs (也, 已经) as `:mod` on the verb.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
The changes target the recurring patterns in the critique. Because the instruction is within about 520 characters of the limit, every edit is short.

1. **Where an entity's full node goes.** "First occurrence in reading order" now says plainly that it means word order in the text, not graph order. Every other mention is a bare variable.
2. **Change-verb rule.** It now says the subject stays `:part-of` on X even when the subject also fills another role. That other role is a re-entrancy, and no inverse `:part` is added.
3. **Modifiers before an apposition noun.** Modifiers written before the apposition noun (的-phrases, 旗下, property words) attach to that noun inside `identity-91 :ARG2`, not to the named entity.
4. **`have-org-role-91` direction.** The title holder is always `:ARG1` (`:ARG1-of` on the person), never `:ARG0`. The verb + 人/者 pattern is marked as a separate case.
5. **Aspect step 1.**
   - Habitual now covers production and distribution practices (printing, issuing) and process nominals that name a routine practice.
   - It applies before step 3.
   - The open choice "`process` or `state`" for content verbs is settled as `process`.

I did not add the `-00` sense rule for a verb morpheme split out of a role noun. The critique rates it low confidence and it rests on one case.

critique
# Review of the instruction: UMR of a whole Chinese document (five sentences)

Costs are counts of the judge's unit verdicts listed above, grouped by error pattern, most costly first. A few gold choices look like noise; the last section names them so the instruction does not chase them.

## 1. Clause structure of copular, purpose and parenthetical constructions (about 20 units: core args event/abstract, peripheral, concepts, temporal, modal)

**What happened**
- **"X 以 Y 为目的" ("X takes Y as its purpose").** The annotator used `have-purpose-91`. Gold uses `identity-91 :ARG1 (目的 :purpose-of <event X>) :ARG2 Y`: the purpose noun is a node, and Y is a plain concept with no aspect or links.
- **A parenthetical restatement ("(their slogan: '…')").** The annotator attached it to the reporting verb as `:medium`. Gold makes it its own clause, `identity-91 :ARG1 <slogan noun> :ARG2 <content event>`, and joins it to the preceding clause with `and`.
- **"X 是 Adj 的" / "X 都是 Adj" ("X is Adj", "X are all Adj") in a claim.** The annotator turned the property word into an event (`Adj-01`). Gold uses `have-mod-91 :ARG1 X :ARG2 Adj`, with the adverb as `:mod` on `have-mod-91`.

**Why it happens.** Section 2.5 tells the annotator to use `have-purpose-91` whenever there is a "marked purpose", so 以…为目的 got caught by it. Nothing in the instruction covers parentheticals. Table 2.3 lists `have-mod-91`, but nothing says the 是…的 frame with a property word belongs to it.

**What to change**
- Limit `have-purpose-91` to purpose clauses (为了, 以便). When the purpose is stated as a noun (以 Y 为目的/目标, "its aim is Y"), use `identity-91`, with the purpose noun carrying `:purpose-of <event>` and Y as `:ARG2`.
- Add: a parenthetical or colon restatement of a sentence element is a separate `identity-91` clause, coordinated with `and`. It is not a `:medium` or `:mod` of the verb.
- Add: in "X 是 Adj (的)" the property word is the `:ARG2` of `have-mod-91`, not a verb sense.

## 2. List-introducing and relational 有 ("has"; about 12 units)

**What happened**
- **"The topics they often report include A, B, C 等".** The annotator built `有-07(topics, list)`. Gold drops 有: the reporting event is the predicate, and the list is `:example` on the topic noun.
- **"A 与 B 有 关系" ("A has a relationship with B").** The annotator wrote `有-01` with B as `:companion`. Gold uses `有-03` with `:ARG0 (and A B)`.
- **等 ("etc.").** The annotator put it as `:mod` on the `and` node. Gold makes it the last `:opN` of the list (twice in this document).

**What to change**
- "N 有 A、B…等" listing examples of a category noun → `:example (and …)` on N. The noun's own clause supplies the predicate.
- "A 与/和 B 有 <relation noun>" → `有-03 :ARG0 (and A B) :ARG1 <noun>`. The 与-partner is a co-argument, never `:companion`.
- 等 / *etc.* closing a list is the final `:opN` of the `and`.

## 3. Shared subjects of aspectual and control verbs, and re-entrant times (about 8 units: reentrancy, core args)

**What happened**
- **Missing control re-entrancies.** Gold gives 继续 ("continue") `:ARG0 <subject>`, and its complement re-enters the same subject. Gold also gives the event nominal under 停止 ("stop") the stopper as `:ARG0`. The annotator left all of these out.
- **Missing re-entrant date.** Gold repeats the clause date as `:temporal` on the second conjunct of `but-91`. The annotator gave the date to the first clause only.

**Why it happens.** The rule "never borrow a participant" in 3.1 is worded so absolutely that the annotator applied it to control verbs as well.

**What to change.** Add an exception to the no-borrowing rule:
- With an aspectual or control verb (继续, 停止, 开始; *continue, stop*), the subject is that verb's `:ARG0` and also re-enters as `:ARG0` of its event complement, including an event nominal that is the complement.
- A time expression that scopes over both clauses of a `but-91` / contrast is attached to both clause events (re-entrancy).

## 4. Aspect (7 units)

**What happened**
- **Event nominal under 停止.** Gold has `process`. The annotator gave `habitual`, as the instruction's step 1 demands.
- **"Survive / exist" verbs.** Gold has `state`; the annotator gave `activity`.
- **Past claim verb (宣称, "claim").** Gold has `performance`; the annotator gave `activity`.
- **Verbal noun used as a predicate's argument (活动, "activity").** Gold has `activity`; the annotator gave `process`.

**What to change**
- In step 1, exclude event nominals that are the complement of an aspectual verb: these are `process`.
- Add existence and survival verbs (生存, 存在, *survive, exist*) to the `state` list.
- A completed past speech act (claim, announce, say) is `performance`.

## 5. Compounds and repeated bare mentions inside a sentence (about 8 units: concept, granularity, coref)

**What happened**
- **Compound noun.** Gold splits a modifier-plus-head compound (a kinship or rank prefix + head noun) into `head :mod prefix`. The annotator kept it as one word.
- **Bare repetition of a name in the same sentence.** Gold gives it its own node (the bare noun) and a `:same-entity` triple. The annotator used a re-entrancy and missed the coref chain (3 coref units).

**What to change**
- Split a compound whose first morpheme is a separable modifier, such as 母-/父-/子- + organisation noun.
- A later short-form mention of a named entity in the same sentence (a bare head noun repeating part of the name) gets its own node with the bare word as concept, plus a `:coref :same-entity` triple. This is an exception to the "within a sentence, use a re-entrancy" rule in 5.3, which applies to pronouns and zero arguments.

## 6. Named entities of fictional or non-human characters, and planets (about 8 units)

**What happened**
- **Named fictional characters.** Gold types them `individual-person`. When a common noun is part of how the character is named (a species word before a proper name), gold puts it in the name as the first `:op`.
- **Planet names.** Gold makes a planet name a named entity of type `planet`. The annotator used the bare noun.

**What to change**
- Named characters, human or not, are `individual-person`.
- Earth, Mars and similar names are `planet` named entities.

## 7. Titles of spouses, sentence adverbs and sequence (about 10 units)

**What happened**
- **First-lady type title.** Gold uses `have-rel-role-91 :ARG3 <title>`, with the country as `:place` on the title noun and "former" as `:mod` on the title. The annotator used `have-org-role-91`.
- **后来 ("later") with 还 ("also").** Gold reifies the sequence as `consecutive :op1 … :op2 …` and makes no separate nodes for the time word.
- **就.** The emphatic or discourse 就 got no node in gold.

**What to change**
- A role defined by marriage or relation (first lady, wife of the president) → `have-rel-role-91`, with the country as `:place` of the role noun and "former" as `:mod` of the role noun.
- Two coordinated predicates linked by 后来 / *then / later* → `consecutive`, with no node for 后来.
- Discourse 就 / 便 in a non-conditional sentence gets no node. Keep the rule that meaningful adverbs (也, 都, 仍) get nodes.

## 8. Modal layer of reported content (about 9 units)

**What happened**
- **Nodes that should not be in the modal layer.** Gold gives no modal parent to plain concepts inside identity clauses (the purpose content, a locative 中 ("in"), a non-event nominal). The annotator gave them modal parents.
- **Who conceives the claim's content.** For the content of a claim, gold makes the claimer the conceiver of every embedded event, including those in the quoted slogan and the later clause about the reports. The annotator put most of these under `author`.
- **Missing `:quote`.** Gold adds `:quote <reporting event>` on the content of reported speech. The annotator never did (4 reentrancy units).

**What to change**
- Under a saying verb, every event of the reported content, including events in an appended slogan or quotation, has the speaker as modal parent. The content's top node also carries `:quote <saying verb>`, and this is to be applied consistently.
- No modal or temporal links for nodes without `:aspect`.

## 9. Temporal over-linking (about 10 units)

**What happened**
- **Links to nodes without aspect.** The annotator linked plain concepts (purpose content, list items such as a travel noun, a locative node).
- **Extra `:after` relation.** It added a link to a habitual relative-clause event (relative clause → creation verb) that gold leaves out.
- **Wrong parents.** It hung reported events on the wrong anchor: gold chains them on the first habitual reporting event, not on the claim verb or on a property word.

**What to change**
- Repeat in 5.1: no temporal parent for any node without `:aspect`.
- Leave out the links between habitual relative-clause events and past performances.
- Under a claim, the embedded habitual event is the local anchor for the other habitual events of the sentence.

## What the annotator got right, which the instruction should keep
- Named entities of works with 《》 kept as name tokens, and no `:wiki` in Chinese.
- Pronoun person and number (`c_refer` was 100%).
- The format of the document level (100%).
- Date `:overlap` anchoring, and the chaining of an aspectual verb to its complement.
- The coref chain from a named periodical to a later pronoun.
- `but-91` with `:ARG1`/`:ARG2` and the modal strength of 可 ("can") as `neutral-affirmative`.
- Superlative modifiers placed on the right noun, and `:frequency` for 经常 ("often").

## Gold choices not to chase
These look like gold noise, so the instruction should not be bent to match them:
- **出现 roles.** Gold reverses the PropBank roles (PropBank says `:ARG0` = location, `:ARG1` = theme). The annotator followed PropBank.
- **领养 sense.** Gold uses `领养-00` although PropBank has `领养-01`.
- **`have-degree-91` roles.** In the headless superlative 其中最大宗 ("the largest of which"), gold numbers the roles differently from the instruction's convention. The only point worth adding: a headless superlative takes an `implicit-argument` head with the classifier as `:unit`, and the partitive 其中 is that superlative's `:ARG5`.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
The edits below cover the critique's recurring patterns. To stay under the 30,000-character limit (the instruction is now at 29,901), I shortened the opening and the guidelines preamble and cut three redundant lines.

**Changes, by critique section:**
- **Purpose, parentheticals, 是…Adj:**
  - `have-purpose-91` is now limited to purpose clauses (为了, 以便).
  - A purpose stated as a noun (以 Y 为目的) becomes `identity-91`, with the purpose noun carrying `:purpose-of`.
  - A parenthetical or colon restatement is its own `identity-91` clause joined by `and`.
  - "X 是 Adj (的)" is `have-mod-91`, never an `Adj-01` event.
- **Lists and 有:**
  - 等 / *etc.* is the last `:opN` of the list.
  - "N 有 A、B…等" listing examples becomes `:example (and …)` on N, with no 有 node.
  - "A 与 B 有 <relation noun>" is `有-03 :ARG0 (and A B)`, never `:companion`.
- **Control verbs:** the no-borrowing rule gets an exception. The subject of an aspectual or control verb re-enters as `:ARG0` of its complement. A time expression over both clauses of a contrast attaches to both events.
- **Aspect:**
  - An event-nominal complement of an aspectual verb is `process`.
  - Existence and survival verbs are `state`.
  - A completed past speech act is `performance`.
- **Modal and temporal:**
  - Every event of reported content (including an appended slogan) takes the speaker as conceiver, and the content's top node gets `:quote`.
  - Nodes without `:aspect` get no temporal or modal links.
  - Habitual relative-clause events are not linked to past performances.
- **Other:**
  - Named characters of any kind are `individual-person`; planet names are `planet` named entities.
  - 后来 joining two predicates becomes `consecutive`, and discourse 就 / 便 gets no node.
  - A later bare short form of a name in the same sentence gets its own node plus a coreference triple.
  - A title held through marriage uses `have-rel-role-91`.

反思 2：17/17 处修改应用上，重标 80.5，保留（v8）
critique
The costliest losses come from how entities and pronouns are tracked and linked: coreference scored F 13, re-entrancy F 44, temporal F 63 and modal F 72. Concepts, aspect and attributes were mostly correct. The problems below are ordered by cost.

## 1. Pronouns and repeated mentions: wrong node, so the coreference chain breaks
**Cost:** coreference R 17 / P 11 (6 of 6 chain units wrong). Also one extra entity, an extra `:ARG0`, an extra possessor re-entrancy, a missing possessor re-entrancy, plus 2 wrong concepts and 4 granularity units.

**What happened:**
- A 3rd-plural pronoun ("their reports", "their slogan") referred to the named periodical in the same sentence. The annotator made a new `person` node for it.
  - Gold re-uses the periodical's variable as the possessor.
  - Gold leaves out the possessive participant of the nominal event ("their reports") entirely.
- The next sentence's "they" was then linked to that bogus `person`, so the whole periodical chain fell apart.
- In the other direction, a shortened second mention of a name (the bare head noun of a periodical's title, used as the whole of a later part-of phrase in the same sentence) was collapsed into the full name's variable. Gold gives it its own node and a `:coref` triple inside the sentence.

**Why:** Rule 5.3 says "within one sentence, coreference is a re-entrancy" without separating pronouns from repeated nouns. Rule 2.4 says every pronoun is a new `person`/`thing` node.

**Change:**
- A pronoun whose antecedent is in the same sentence (including an organisation or publication referred to by 他们 or *they*) gets no node of its own. Re-use the antecedent's variable.
- A possessive pronoun on a nominal event does not become that event's `:ARG0`.
- A pronoun across sentences is a new node linked to the antecedent entity (here, the organisation), not to another pronoun node.
- A word that repeats a name or noun overtly (a short name, a bare head noun) always gets its own node. If it refers to an entity already in the same sentence, add a `:coref` `:same-entity` triple. Re-entrancy is only for pronouns and dropped or controlled arguments.

## 2. "虽然 … 不过/但是" in one sentence
**Cost:** a wrong root, the two missing `:ARG1`/`:ARG2` links, and the knock-on effects on temporal and modal parents.

**What happened:** The annotator used `:concession` on the main clause. With both markers in the same sentence, gold uses `but-91` with `:ARG1` = the 虽然 clause(s) and `:ARG2` = the 不过 clause. It also put an extra `:mod` 都 on the root; gold has no such node.

**Why:** Rule 2.5 maps 虽然 to `:concession` and says nothing about the paired form.

**Change:** When a concessive marker (虽然, 尽管, *although*) is followed by 但是/不过/却 in the same sentence, use `but-91 :ARG1 <concessive clause> :ARG2 <main clause>`. Keep `:concession` for unpaired 虽然.

## 3. `:quote` on reported content is skipped
**Cost:** 5 missing re-entrancy edges.

**What happened:** Every top node of reported content needs `:quote` pointing to the reporting verb. This covers each conjunct of a reported consecutive or `and` chain, and the content of a quoted slogan inside an `identity-91` (there the `:quote` points to that `identity-91`). The annotator added none of these.

**Why:** Rule 3 calls `:quote` something "the UMR release data also marks", which sounds optional.

**Change:** Make it mandatory. Every top event of reported or quoted content (including passive "被指/被称", "is said to"), and each of its conjuncts, gets `:quote <reporting event>`. The content of a quoted slogan gets `:quote` on the frame that introduces it.

## 4. Rules already in the instruction but not applied
**Cost:** 3 missing re-entrancy edges (in a 3-of-6 re-entrancy total).

**What happened:**
- **Control with an event nominal:** the subject of 停止 was not re-entered as `:ARG0` of its nominal complement.
- **Shared time expression:** a date scoping over both halves of a `but-91` was not attached to the second clause too.
- **Consecutive chain with one subject:** in a 后来 chain whose clauses share a subject, gold re-enters that subject as the `:ARG0` of the later verb. Gold also gives the 还 in "后来还" no node. The annotator did neither, which follows the instruction's ban on dropped-subject re-entrancy.

**Change:**
- Put the first two rules in the checklist so they are applied.
- Add an exception to the no-borrowing rule: in a `consecutive` (后来) chain, a dropped subject of the later clause re-enters the first clause's subject.
- 还/也 directly after 后来 gets no node.

## 5. Frequency adverbs and location postpositions
**Cost:** 2 wrong peripheral labels, and the peripheral-event check scored F 50.

**What happened:** 经常 and 重复 should be `:frequency`. The annotator used `:mod` and `:manner`.

**Change:** Add a rule: frequency adverbs (经常, 常常, 往往, 重复, 屡次; *often, repeatedly*) → `:frequency`. Also note that 3.1 makes time adverbs `:temporal`; frequency adverbs are their own class.

**Locations:**
- "在 N 中/上/里" should be a postposition concept: `(中 :op1 N)`. The annotator dropped the postposition.
- For appearance and existence verbs whose roleset has a location argument (出现), the location is a numbered argument, not `:place`.

**Change:** Extend the 上 rule (in 3.1) to every location postposition: (`中`/`上`/`里` `:op1 N`). Tell the annotator to check the roleset for a location argument before using `:place`.
- Note that gold here gave the theme `:ARG0` and the location `:ARG1`, the reverse of the PropBank glosses. Flag this verb class like the belong-type note: follow gold practice, not the glosses.

## 6. Named characters and a noun before a name
**Cost:** 2 wrong concepts, 2 granularity units, 2 name-token units, 1 extra `identity-91`, and an extra cross-sentence coreference.

**What happened:** Named fictional characters were typed `person`; they should be `individual-person`. A category noun written right before a name (alien + name) was reified as an `identity-91` apposition. Gold either puts the noun inside the name or uses it as the entity's type concept.

**Change:**
- Every named individual, fictional or not, is `individual-person` unless a category noun right before the name serves as its type.
- A bare category noun right before a name (no 的, no title) is not an apposition: use it as the type concept, or as the first `:op` of the name.
- Reserve `identity-91` for descriptive noun phrases.

## 7. Temporal anchor and its parents in multi-clause sentences
**Cost:** about 8 temporal units.

**What happened:**
- **Anchor choice:** In a two-clause `and`, gold anchors on the first clause's event and hangs the second on it with `:overlap`. The annotator anchored on the later verb.
- **Reported clause:** The reported event links to the saying verb. A `have-mod-91` or `identity-91` that frames it gets no temporal parent. Later reported or habitual events `:overlap` that first content event, not the saying verb.
- **Habitual relative clause:** A habitual relative-clause verb on an object got a temporal link; gold gives it none.

**Change:**
- In coordination, the anchor is the first conjunct's main event.
- Abstract predicates (`have-mod-91`, `identity-91`) never get a temporal parent, even inside reported content. Their eventive argument takes the matrix verb as parent.

## 8. Modal parents of reported content
**Cost:** about 7 modal units.

**What happened:**
- In the sentence with a slogan and a concessive, gold gives the speaker as a modal parent for the main reported event and the slogan's event. For the main claim's `have-mod-91` and the slogan's event, gold also adds an `author :full-affirmative` link.
- The slogan's `identity-91` has only `author` as parent.

**Change:** Keep speaker → content. Add `author` as a second parent for the content of a claim the author reports and then contrasts. Give the frame (`identity-91`) of a parenthetical quotation `author` as its parent.

## 9. Word-level concept choices
**Cost:** a few units each.

- **Fixed word vs. its first character:** For a word in PropBank as a whole (e.g. *X-是*), use that roleset, not the roleset of its first character. Look up the full word first.
- **Classifier in an adjective:** In a compound like 最大宗, the classifier is a `:unit` and the property is the adjective alone. The degree frame takes the property as `:ARG1` and the degree word as `:ARG2`, and 其中 goes on it as `:ARG5`. Gold's unusual role order here is a convention worth stating.
- **Unnamed omitted head:** An omitted head noun is `implicit-argument`, not `thing`.
- **Named celestial bodies:** These are named entities (`planet`, …).
- **Bound modifiers in compounds:** A bound modifier glued to a noun (母公司) is split into head + `:mod` when gold splits it, as for other modifier + head compounds.
- **Activity, not process:** A verb-nominal used as a predicate argument and describing an ongoing activity got `process`; gold uses `activity`.

## What the instruction should keep
These parts worked and should stay as they are:
- Chinese name splitting and title marks in names; `newspaper` as the periodical type.
- `have-rel-role-91` for first lady, with `:place` and `前` as `:mod`.
- `identity-91` with `目的 :purpose-of` for a purpose stated as a noun.
- `:example` (with 等 as the last `:op`) for "N 有 A、B等".
- The `but-91` with `:part-of` for an edition noun.
- Habitual aspect for publishing and reporting.
- `performance` for completed speech acts.
- The date `:overlap` and `document-creation-time :before` pattern.
- The modal frame: speaker as parent for reported content, `neutral-affirmative` for 可.

Person, number and other attributes and the document format scored 100. Concept, sense and aspect choices were at 88–95.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
**Summary of changes.** The instruction was at the 30,000-character limit, so I first freed space. I removed redundant text: the generic intro paragraph, the long two-level overview, the entity-type list, a duplicated decade rule, a generic self-check bullet and the "precision" line. The new rules target the costliest problems in the critique:

1. **Coreference within a sentence (largest cost).** The old rule treated every same-sentence coreference as re-entrancy. It now splits two cases:
   - A pronoun or dropped argument re-uses its antecedent's variable. This includes 他们/*they* used for an organisation or publication.
   - An overtly repeated name or noun gets its own node plus a `:same-entity` triple.
   - A possessive pronoun on an event nominal is omitted.
   - A pronoun in a later sentence links to the antecedent entity.
   - The checklist line is updated to match.
2. **Paired 虽然/尽管 … 但是/不过/却.** In one sentence this now gives `but-91`; unpaired 虽然 keeps `:concession`.
3. **`:quote` is mandatory.** It goes on the top event of reported or quoted content and on each of its conjuncts, including passive reporting. A quoted slogan's content takes `:quote` on its framing node.
4. **后来 chains.** 还/也 right after 后来 gets no node, and a dropped later subject re-enters the first clause's subject.
5. **Existing rules made visible.** The control-verb re-entrancy and the shared time expression over both halves of `but-91` are added to the checklist.
6. **Frequency and location.**
   - Frequency adverbs → `:frequency`.
   - Every location postposition becomes `(中 :op1 N)`.
   - Check the roleset for a location argument before using `:place`.
7. **Named characters.** Fictional named characters are `individual-person`. A bare category noun right before a name is the type concept, not an apposition.
8. **Temporal anchoring.** In a coordination, the anchor is the first conjunct's event. `have-mod-91` and `identity-91` get no temporal parent, even inside reported content; their eventive argument takes the matrix verb as parent.
9. **Omitted head noun.** It is `implicit-argument`, not `thing`.

critique
I've ordered the problems by how many judged units they cost. Each one has the cost, why it happened, and a general rule to change or add in the instruction.

## 1. Coreference: too many links, and a repeated name given its own node (j_coref P 33; about 9 units, plus a cascade into entity, argument and reentrancy checks)
**Cost:**
- Two category nouns were linked across sentences: a generic kind noun that appears in an example list and again in a later sentence.
- A fictional character mentioned in two sentences was linked. Gold links neither case.
- Inside a quoted slogan in a parenthesis, the publication's name came back without its title marks. The annotator gave it a new node plus `:same-entity`. Gold re-uses the publication's variable.
- That one extra node cost 1 entity_found unit, 1 partial core argument, 2 missing re-entrancies and 4 partial coref chains.

**Why:** Section 5.3 says "an overt repeated name … gets its own node plus `:same-entity`". It never limits coreference to tracked participants with a definite referent.

**Change:**
- A repeated name inside a slogan, gloss, parenthesis or quote in the same sentence that refers to an entity already in that sentence is a re-entrancy, not a new node.
- Do not corefer generic or kind-denoting nouns (bare nouns naming a category, members of an example list), even when the same word recurs.
- Do not corefer a named entity that appears only as an example or list member in one sentence with a later mention, unless the text treats it as a discourse topic.
- Never link a `name` node: the annotator did this once.

## 2. Modal parents for reported content (i_modal; 7 units)
**Cost:**
- **Active reporting verb with a clause object:** the annotator gave the content's events only the speaker as conceiver. Gold gives each content event **both** `(author :full-affirmative e)` and `(speaker :full-affirmative e)`.
- **Later clauses about the same source:** gold also gives the speaker as an extra parent to the restating slogan clause and to the "but" clause about that source's reports.
- **Event nominal inside the content:** a nominal used as the content's argument (not its top) is author-only in gold. The annotator gave it the speaker.
- **Passive reporting verb with no agent:** for the 被指 type, gold does not use the reporting verb as conceiver. It uses the content's subject node, with `(author :full-affirmative <that node>)`. The annotator put the verb in the conceiver slot.

**Change:** Rewrite the reported-speech rule in 5.2:
- The content's predicates get both author and speaker as parents.
- Event nominals inside the content stay with author only.
- When a passive reporting verb has no overt speaker, the conceiver is the content's subject node. That node gets `(author :full-affirmative X)`. Never use the reporting event as conceiver.

## 3. Temporal links inside "but" sentences and reported content (h_temporal 71; 5 units, plus 1 reentrancy)
**Cost:**
- In a past "stopped X, but Y still continues" sentence, the annotator linked the second clause with `:after`. Gold uses `:overlap`.
- The fronted date was not re-entered on the second clause. The instruction already says a time over both halves of but-91 attaches to both, but this was not followed.
- In the reported-content sentence, the slogan clause and the later "but" clause were hung on the reporting verb. Gold hangs them on the first event inside the content: the topic event that the later clauses restate.
- An absolute present judgement with a "can be counted as" verb was given `:overlap` to document-creation-time. Gold uses `:before`.

**Change:**
- In a but-91 or contrast with "still / continue", the continuing clause `:overlap`s the first clause. Never use `:after`.
- Put the date-reentrancy rule in the main body, not only the checklist, and state it is mandatory when the date opens the sentence.
- When later clauses restate or qualify the content of a report, their events take the content's main event as parent, not the reporting verb.

## 4. Superlative nominal with a dropped head (have-degree-91; about 7 units)
**Cost:** The case is a "superlative + adjective + classifier" compound used as the subject, with a partitive "among them" word before it. The annotator kept it as one concept with `:mod` partitive. Gold has:
- `implicit-argument` as the head, with `:unit` set to the classifier;
- `:ARG1-of (have-degree-91 :ARG1 <adjective> :ARG2 <superlative word> :ARG5 <partitive>)`.

**Why:** The instruction contradicts gold three ways:
- It says "do not use `:ARG5`".
- It puts 最 in `:ARG3`.
- It says a partitive word is `:mod`.

**Change:** Add a case. A superlative compound with no head noun (最 + adjective + classifier) is split as gold does above. The partitive word (其中, *among them*) is the comparison set, `:ARG5`, not `:mod`. Limit the "partitive is `:mod`" rule to cases with no degree word.

## 5. Control and argument roles (d_core 86, d_peripheral_event 71)
- **Control not applied:** the subject of a stopping verb was not re-entered as `:ARG0` of its event-nominal complement (publication). The instruction already has this control rule; put it in the checklist, explicitly including nominal complements and the stopping verb.
- **Appearance verb (出现 type):** the annotator followed PropBank (location = ARG0). Gold puts the appearing entity in `:ARG0` and the "in N 中" location in `:ARG1`. State this gold convention, as the instruction already does for belong-type rolesets.
- **Quantity word on an event nominal:** a "most of" quantity word on an event nominal is `:mod` in gold, not `:quant`.
- **Relative-clause head:** when the noun is the object of a relative clause (*the topics they often report*), gold makes the verb the clause's main conjunct and the noun its `:ARG1`. The annotator put the noun at the top with `:ARG1-of`. Add a rule: in "N that X V-s 有 A, B…" (topic sentences), the reported verb heads the clause and N is its `:ARG1`.
- **Missing `:quote`:** the slogan's content event did not get `:quote <its identity-91 framing node>`. The instruction already says this; give an example.

## 6. Aspect (c_aspect 89; 2 units)
- **State verb under "continue":** a survive/exist verb under a continuation verb was given `activity`. Step 2 already lists 生存 as `state`. Add that this holds even under 继续 and 仍.
- **Activity noun:** an activity noun as the predicate complement of a judging verb is `activity` in gold, not `process`. Narrow step 3 (process nominals) to nominals that are arguments of light or experiential verbs or are the subject/object of eventive verbs, not complements of "count as / be".

## 7. Smaller items
- **Bound-morpheme compounds:** a compound made of a bound modifier morpheme and a full noun (parent + company type) splits into the noun with `:mod` the morpheme. Add this to 2.1.
- **Planet names:** a well-known planet name used as a place is a named entity: `(planet :name …)`.
- **Fictional character in an example list:** a character written as "category noun + foreign name" was `individual-person` in gold, with the category noun inside the name. The same character in a later sentence was category noun + `:name`. The gold is inconsistent here, so this is low priority; at most, prefer `individual-person` for named fictional characters in lists.
- **Sense for 领养:** the predicate has a PropBank roleset (`-01`), but gold used `-00`. The cost is one unit; no rule change is advised.

## Keep
- The 以…为目的 purpose-noun identity rule: matched exactly.
- The `have-rel-role-91` rule for a title held through marriage, and `consecutive` with the dropped subject re-entered: both correct.
- The `but-91` rule for a 虽然…不过 sentence (the "although" clause inside `:ARG1`): correct.
- Title marks inside the name, the classifier and example-list rules (`:example (and … 等)`), and `:quote` on each conjunct of reported content: all correct.
- The habitual aspect for a publication's reporting practice, and `performance` for a completed past claim: correct.
- Pronoun handling (refer-person, refer-number; `c_refer` 100) and the event concepts (100): keep as written.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
**Summary of changes**

These edits target the critique's recurring problems. Space is freed by cutting text that repeats other sections.

1. **Coreference (largest cost).**
   - Coreference is limited to tracked entities. Generic or kind nouns, members of example lists, and names given only as examples are never linked.
   - A repeated name inside a slogan, gloss or parenthesis of the same sentence re-uses the existing variable instead of getting a new node.
2. **Modal links for reported content.**
   - Each predicate in the content gets both the author and the speaker as modal parents.
   - Event nominals inside the content get the author only.
   - A passive reporting verb with no speaker uses the content's subject as conceiver, never the reporting event.
3. **Temporal links.**
   - A date that opens a but-91 or contrast sentence attaches to both clauses.
   - A "still / continue" clause `:overlap`s the first clause, never `:after`.
   - Clauses that restate or qualify a report's content hang on the content's main event, not on the reporting verb.
4. **Superlative with no head noun.**
   - The pattern is `implicit-argument` with the classifier as `:unit`, under `have-degree-91` with `:ARG5` for the partitive word.
   - The general ban on `:ARG5` is lifted, and the partitive-as-`:mod` rule now has an exception for this case.
5. **Appearance verbs.** The gold convention is stated: the appearing entity is `:ARG0` and the location is `:ARG1`.
6. **Aspect.**
   - State verbs stay `state` under 继续/仍.
   - An activity noun that is the complement of a judging verb is `activity`.
7. **Trimmed for space:**
   - the intro sentence about scoring;
   - the opening line of section 1;
   - the duplicate `:degree` bullet;
   - the AMR type list;
   - the verbose "Then every event" bullet;
   - a duplicate checklist line.

critique
Below are the error patterns, most costly first. For each I give its cost (the judge's checks and about how many units), why it happened, and the change to the instruction.

## 1. Quoted article titles were turned into event structures instead of named publications (about 35 units)
**Cost:** a_entity_concept, f_name_tokens (all the missing names), extra events and entities, d_core_args_abstract, c_other_attributes (stray `:quant`), and the extra temporal, modal, reentrancy and coref triples hung on those invented nodes. This hit three of the five sentences.

**Why:** A title in 「…」 after a count of articles ("one piece of"), or set beside a news or article noun, is the name of a work in the gold. It is `publication :name`, with every word as an `:opN`, the opening and closing 「 」 included. The instruction covers only 《》 titles. So the annotator broke each title into predicates, with names, quantities, role reifications, `:quote` and conceivers inside it. All of that was extra.

**Change:**
- Add a rule: "A quoted headline or article title in 「」 or “” that names an article, used with a classifier or beside an article or news noun, is `(p / publication :name (n / name :op1 "「" … :opN "」"))`. Every word of the title, punctuation included, is an `:opN`. Nothing inside it is analysed: no events, no entities, no `:quote`, no temporal, modal or coref triples. The classifier and number go on the publication as `:unit`/`:quant`."
- When the title is in apposition to a noun ("the article 「…」"), use `(noun :ARG1-of (i / identity-91 :ARG2 publication :aspect state))`. That `identity-91` gets the author as its modal parent and no temporal parent.
- Keep the existing reported-speech analysis only for a quote that is the direct content of a verb of saying or reporting, with no classifier.

## 2. Compound words that should be split into head + modifier (about 15 units)
**Cost:** a_entity_concept and d_peripheral (missing `:mod`) wherever these words appear. Several of the judge's mismatches (one node matched to an unrelated `:mod` node in two sentences) come from the same cause.

**Why:** The gold splits words built as a demonstrative plus a one-character noun, "all/whole" plus a noun, and a verb plus 者/人:
- demonstrative + noun → `noun :mod demonstrative`;
- whole/all + noun → `noun :mod whole/all`;
- verb + 者 for an agent → `者 :ARG0-of verb`;
- verb + 人 for a patient ("cloned person") → `人 :ARG1-of verb`.

The instruction has a verb + 人/者 rule only for the agent case, and it was not applied here. The patient case and the demonstrative case are not mentioned at all.

**Change:**
- Extend 2.2/2.4: "Split a word made of a demonstrative or totality prefix plus a noun into the noun with `:mod` of the prefix. Split verb + 者/人 into 者/人 with `:ARG0-of` (agent) or `:ARG1-of` (patient, e.g. the thing produced) of the verb. A verb not in PropBank is `-00`. The verb gets `:aspect` (state for a disposition, process for a kind), an `:overlap` temporal link to the clause verb, and the author as its modal parent."
- Add a checklist item that names this rule.

## 3. Attributive property words were `:mod` instead of events (about 15 units)
**Cost:** b_event_sense, c_aspect (missing), d_core_args_event, d_peripheral_entity, h_temporal, i_modal.

**Why:** The instruction's last bullet of 3.1 ("a property word used attributively is a `:mod` concept with no aspect and no links") is too broad. In the gold, an attributive modifier that has a Chinese PropBank roleset is an event attached by an inverse role:
- property predicates with an "entity described" `:ARG0` (e.g. 显著-01, 真实-01) → `noun :ARG0-of (x / word-01 :aspect state)`;
- verbs that produce something (e.g. 合成-01) → `noun :ARG1-of (x / verb-01 :aspect performance)`.

Each of these gets an `:overlap` temporal link to the clause event and the author as its modal parent. Only words with no roleset (distinguishing or relational words such as "diplomatic", "moral") stay `:mod`.

**Change:**
- Rewrite that bullet: "Look the modifier up in PropBank. If it has a roleset, annotate it as an event with an inverse role, using the role the roleset gives the described entity. Otherwise use `:mod`."
- Also: an event nominal that modifies a noun (an "X's handshake photo" kind) is `:mod`, with `process` aspect, not `:topic`.

## 4. The modal and temporal treatment of reports by a publication (about 14 units in i_modal and h_temporal)
**What went wrong:**
- **Who is the conceiver.** In the gold, when a publication or other source is the subject of a series of reporting verbs, the source is the conceiver of those reporting verbs: author → source, then source → each reporting verb. Each content event gets only the author as its parent. The annotator did the reverse: author → reporting verb, and source → content.
- **Temporal links in the content.**
  - A past event inside reported content took the reporting verb as its temporal parent, with `:before`. It was not linked to its date.
  - Dates inside the content got no temporal parent.
  - A means or support clause inside the content `:overlap`s its event. The annotator used `:after`.
- **No links for complement events in the content.** An event that is the complement of the content's predicate (e.g. "support X to become president") got no aspect and no modal link.

**Why:** The instruction (5.2) says content predicates get both the author and the speaker as parents. The date rule (5.1) also competes with "an event in a complement clause takes its matrix event as parent".

**Change:**
- State the source-as-conceiver pattern for publications and organisations that report.
- State an order of precedence: "Inside reported content, the matrix reporting verb is the temporal parent (`:before` for a past event it reports). A date inside the content is a `:temporal` role only and gets no document-level link."

## 5. Verb + complement compounds, senses and constructions with 有 and 靠 (about 10 units)
- **Directional or resultative complements.** A verb with such a complement is one concept when PropBank lists the compound (e.g. 点出-01, 贴到-01), even when it is split over two tokens. Use the compound roleset's own roles: for the posting verb, `:ARG1` is the place and `:ARG2` is the thing posted. The annotator had these reversed.
- **"Have the ability to V".** This is `有-06 :ARG1 (能力 :ARG1-of (identity-91 :ARG2 V-event :aspect state))`. It is not `:mod`.
  - The `identity-91` gets the author as its modal parent.
  - The inner event's `neutral-affirmative` comes from the author, not from 有.
- **Relying on a supporter.** "Rely on X('s support) to achieve Y" (靠 X) is `Y :reason X-event` with no node for the reliance verb.
- **Choosing senses.** Add: "Pick the sense whose role glosses fit (有-06 for an ability or an attribute held). Use `-00` for a word that is not in PropBank." The annotator gave `-01` to words PropBank does not list.

## 6. Named events with a year in the name (about 6 units)
A dated election or another named event ("the 2000 presidential election") is `(e / event :name (n / name :op1 "2000" :op2 "年" :op3 …))`. It is not a process noun with a `date-entity`, and it gets no temporal or modal links. Add this to 2.2.

## 7. Example sentences and discourse frames (about 7 units)
- **Sentence-initial "for example".** An opening 如/例如 that offers the sentence as an example of the previous claim is `(h / have-example-91 :ARG1 (i / implicit-predicate) :ARG2 <main event>)`. Add this to 2.5.
- **but-91.** Discourse frames get no modal link. The temporal anchor of a but-91 is its `:ARG1` clause: document-creation-time `:before` for a past-tense description. The `:ARG2` clause `:overlap`s it. The annotator anchored on `:ARG2` and used `:overlap` with document-creation-time.
- **Parts of a publication.** The contents or articles of a publication are `:part-of` the publication, not `:possessor`. Extend the component rule in 3.1 to cover this.

## 8. Purpose clauses and adverbs (about 6 units)
- **为了 clauses.** For 为了 with a shared subject, the gold re-enters the main subject as the purpose event's `:ARG0`. The rule "never fill the agent of a purpose clause" is too absolute. The gold also used `have-reason-91` with no aspect and no modal link.
  - Make the agent rule depend on the subject being shared.
  - Drop the instruction to give the frame `:aspect state` and `(author :full-affirmative h)`.
  - Treat the frame's name as uncertain until other gold data confirm it.
- **Adverbs.** Additive and escalating adverbs that link clauses (还 and 也 in a list of acts, "even" 甚至) got no node in the gold. Narrow "every adverb gets a node" to adverbs that scope over a single predicate.
- **Coreference of repeated country names.** Do not corefer two mentions of a country name inside one sentence when one or both are only modifiers.

## What to keep
The annotator did these well, and the instruction should keep the rules behind them:
- **Structure:** event detection (98 F), granularity (100), format (100), and pronoun person/number (100).
- **Discourse frames:** the `and` frame for chains of reporting verbs, and but-91 for 虽然…但.
- **Classifiers:** classifiers kept as `:unit` with `:quant`.
- **Past events:** `performance` aspect for completed past acts, and document-creation-time `:before` for past sentence anchors.
- **Coreference:** pronouns linked to the publication.
- **Habitual aspect:** `habitual` for a recurring editorial practice.
- **Reported content:** the reported-content analysis for a verb of reporting with a direct clause object, with `:quote` on the content's top event.
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
I made changes only for the critique's most costly patterns, and freed room by trimming redundant or niche text, since the instruction was close to the 30000-character limit.

**What I add or change:**
1. **Quoted article titles (about 35 units).** A title in 「」 or “” used with a classifier, or next to an article or news noun, is now a `publication` name. Every word and mark of the title is an `:opN`, and nothing inside it is analysed. I also added named events with a year in the name: `event :name`, with no links.
2. **Compound words (about 15 units).**
   - A verb + 人/者 word is split, with `:ARG0-of` for the agent and `:ARG1-of` for a patient or product.
   - The inner verb gets an aspect, an `:overlap` link to the clause verb, and the author as its modal parent.
   - A demonstrative or totality prefix + noun is split into the noun with a `:mod` of the prefix.
3. **Attributive modifiers (about 15 units).** A modifier that has a PropBank roleset is now an event attached by an inverse role, with links. Only words with no roleset stay a plain `:mod`. An event nominal that modifies a noun is `:mod` with `process` aspect. I adjusted the "Not events" line in 2.1 so it agrees with this.
4. **Smaller discourse fixes.**
   - A sentence-opening 如/例如 is `have-example-91`.
   - The temporal anchor of but-91 is its `:ARG1` event.
   - Discourse frames get no modal link.
   - A 为了 clause that shares the main subject re-enters it as `:ARG0`, and the no-borrowing rule is narrowed to match.
   - The articles or contents of a publication are `:part-of` it.
5. **"Has the ability to V" and 靠 X.** Added `有-06` with an `identity-91` on 能力 for the ability case, and `:reason` with no node for 靠.

**What I leave out:** the critique's publication-as-conceiver modal pattern. It contradicts the reported-speech rules validated on batch 3, and its own guidance on dates is ambiguous.

**What I trim to make room:**
- The event-type examples in 2.1.
- The role-noun examples, which the 2.2 rule and the table already cover.
- The mixed-separator rule.
- Wording in the relative-clause-with-aspectual-verb bullet, the fused-negation rule and the fame rule.
- The checklist, which I merge.

反思 2：18/26 处修改应用上，重标 77.0，保留（v11）
critique
The costliest losses come from how the instruction handles reported speech, time phrases and noun phrases that hide an extra frame. The perfect scores (coreference chains, person/number on pronouns, document format) show the basics should stay. Problems are ordered by cost, most costly first.

## 1. Modal links for a series of reports by one source (≈9 modal units, plus 3 reentrancy units)
**What happened:** A periodical was the subject of several coordinated reporting verbs (report, say, claim). The annotator gave each reporting verb an author link, and gave each predicate of the reported content two links: one from the author and one from the periodical. Gold does it the other way round:
- the source entity gets `(author :full-affirmative src)`;
- each reporting verb gets `(src :full-affirmative verb)`;
- the content's predicates get an author link only.

Gold also puts `:quote <reporting verb>` on every event of the content, nested reason events included. The annotator only put it on the content's top event.

**Why:** Section 5.2 tells the annotator to give the content "both" links and to give the speaker an author link. It never says that the reporting act itself sits under the speaker.

**Change:** Rewrite the reported-speech rule:
- the speaker node is under the author;
- every reporting or claiming verb with that speaker as subject has the speaker as its modal parent;
- content predicates get the author only.

Extend the `:quote` rule to every event inside the content (reason, manner and complement events too).

## 2. Time phrases: "named event + 时" and "clause + 时" (≈12 units across concepts, names, entities, temporal and peripheral checks)
**What happened:**
- **Year + event noun + 时:** The annotator built a 时 node over the event noun with a separate `date-entity`. Gold makes the whole phrase a named `event` (year, 年 and event noun as `:opN`), used directly as `:temporal`, with no 时 node, no date node and no temporal link. The main verb then links to `document-creation-time` directly.
- **Clause + 时:** Gold uses the clause's event itself as `:temporal`, again with no 时 node.

**Why:** The annotator extended the postposition rule (在 N 中 → `中 :op1 N`) to 时. The named-event rule exists but has no trigger for this case.

**Change:**
- Add: "时 / 的时候 after a clause or event noun gets no node; the event itself is `:temporal`."
- Add: "year + 年 + event noun is a named event; never split off a date-entity."
- Add: a date inside reported content gets no temporal parent. The content event takes the reporting verb as parent (`:before` for a past event claimed later), not the date.

## 3. A noun with a content complement, and a news noun with a quoted title (≈10 units)
**Ability-type noun + verb phrase** (have the ability to X):
- Gold: `noun :ARG1-of (identity-91 :ARG2 event)`, with `:aspect state` and an author modal link. The event gets `(author :neutral-affirmative event)`, not a link from 有.
- Annotator: `:mod event`, with the modal parent set to the 有 verb.

**Measure + news/article noun + 「title」:**
- Gold: the news noun is the head. It carries `:quant`/`:unit` and `:part-of` the periodical, and is `:ARG1-of identity-91 :ARG2 (publication :name …)` with `:aspect state` and an author link.
- Annotator: made the publication the head and moved the news noun, the quantity and the owner onto it.

**Why:** Section 2.2 makes any quoted title "next to an article/news noun" the publication itself. It also says an apposition identity-91 gets no aspect and no links.

**Change:**
- Keep "publication with quant/unit" only for a classifier + quoted title with no common noun.
- When a common noun is present, that noun is the head, and identity-91 links it to the titled publication.
- This identity-91, and the "ability/right/chance to X" identity, take `:aspect state` and an author modal link (no temporal link). The no-aspect rule should apply only to apposition on a named entity.
- An ability complement gets author `neutral-affirmative`.

## 4. Unsplit compounds and attributive predicates (≈10 units)
The annotator kept several kinds of compound whole that gold splits:
- **Verb/adjective + 者:** Gold uses `者 :ARG0-of (X-00 :aspect state)`. Section 2.2 names only 人/者 after a verb, so an adjective-like stem was not split.
- **Verb + 人, where the person undergoes the verb:** Gold uses `人 :ARG1-of (V :aspect process)`.
- **全 + noun:** Gold uses `noun :mod 全`.
- **Attributive adjective that has a roleset:** Gold uses `:ARG0-of (adj-01 :aspect state)`, with an overlap link to the event it modifies and an author link. The annotator used a plain `:mod`, although section 3.1 already says to check PropBank first.

**Change:**
- State the split rule generally: any stem before 人/者 that is a predicate (verb or adjective) becomes an event. Use `:ARG0-of` if the person does or has it, `:ARG1-of` if it is done to them.
- Split 全/各/该-type prefixes as `:mod`.
- Repeat in the checklist: "every attributive adjective: look up its roleset before writing `:mod`."

## 5. Adverbs that only chain clauses (≈7 extra nodes and peripheral units)
**What happened:** The annotator gave nodes to 还 and 甚至 opening a later conjunct, and to 也 in a 但…也 clause or a reported clause. Gold drops them all; it keeps 也 only where it links to a previous sentence.

**Why:** Section 3.1 says "every adverb that carries meaning gets its own node."

**Change:** Add an exception: 还, 甚至, and 也 that only mark a clause as additional or climactic relative to another clause of the same sentence (a coordination chain or a but-91 second half) get no node.

## 6. Verbs that express means or reason, and verb concepts (≈8 units)
- **靠/凭/通过 N (by relying on N) + main verb:** Gold has no node for 靠-type verbs; N or its event becomes `:reason` of the main verb. The annotator made a `靠-01 :manner` event, which brought an extra node, reentrancy, temporal and modal links. Add this as a rule.
- **Missing senses:** Words missing from PropBank must be `-00`. The annotator wrote `-01` twice without checking.
- **Verb + result word:** A verb plus its result complement written as one token (V到) is one concept, `V到-01`.
- **Sense of 有:** having an ability takes a different 有 sense from having or owning something.

Make the instruction say: "write `-00` unless `propbank_lookup` returned that exact roleset."

## 7. Purpose frame, frame modals, and the aspect of purpose events (≈5 units)
**What gold did:**
- Used `have-reason-91` for 为了 + clause.
- Gave the reified frame no `:aspect` and no modal link.
- Gave but-91 no modal link either.
- Gave the purpose event `performance` aspect, because it was carried out in a past report.

**Instruction conflicts:** Section 2.5 says to give both frames `:aspect state` and an author link, and section 4.1 says a purpose is `activity`.

**Change:**
- Discourse frames (but-91, contrast-91, have-reason-91, have-purpose-91) take no aspect and no modal link.
- A purpose that was actually carried out in a past narrative takes the aspect of the main event.
- Mention that gold treats 为了 clauses as `have-reason-91`.

## 8. Non-core roles of noun modifiers (≈6 units)
| Modifier | Gold role | Annotator's role |
|---|---|---|
| Content or part of a publication | `:part-of` | `:possessor` |
| Issue or matter "of" a subject (问题 of X) | `:topic` | `:possessor` |
| Domain noun on a policy-type noun (外交 政策) | `:topic` | `:mod` |
| Named legislative body as the location of a group | `building :place` | organization as `:mod` |

Extend the section 3.1 role list with these.

## 9. Temporal links
**Coordinated clauses:** Gold chains the conjuncts in sequence (op1 → op2 → op3), with each later conjunct `:overlap` the previous one. The annotator hung them all on op1. Change "link the other events to the anchor" to chain them.

**Relative-clause events:** A participle on a noun (synthesised photo) `:overlap`s the clause verb rather than coming `:before` it. The event nominal inside it hangs on that participle.

**Characterising states:** In a document narrating a past entity, characterising states take `(document-creation-time :before e)`, not `:overlap`.

## 10. Example sentences
A sentence opened by 如/例如 that illustrates the previous one is `have-example-91 :ARG1 (implicit-predicate) :ARG2 <main event>`. The annotator dropped 如 entirely. Add this to section 2.5.

## Keep
- Coreference: each mention links to the nearest earlier mention, and same-sentence pronouns re-use the antecedent's variable (100% on chains).
- Pronouns as `thing`/`person` with person and number.
- Bare classifier + 「」 titles as `publication` with `:quant`/`:unit` and the 「」 marks as `:opN`.
- `individual-person` for named people, with no `:wiki` in Chinese documents.
- `document-creation-time :before` on the anchor of past narrative sentences.
- `process` for event nominals that modify a noun.
- `performance` for completed past participles.
- Core-argument choice (core arguments of events about 94%, core role labels 97%).
reflect（说明和提出的修改）
Summary of the changes, ordered by cost in the critique. To stay under the length limit, I cut some narrow rules from earlier batches and the redundant checklist lines.

1. **Reported speech.** The modal rule is rewritten: the speaker is under the author, and each reporting or claiming verb hangs on the speaker. Content predicates get an author link only. `:quote` now goes on every event of the content, not just the top event.
2. **Time phrases.**
   - 时 / 的时候 after a clause or event noun gets no node; the event itself is `:temporal`.
   - Year + 年 + event noun is one named event, with no date-entity.
   - A date inside reported content gets no temporal parent; the content event hangs on the reporting verb.
3. **Titles and ability nouns.**
   - A quoted title is a publication name only after a bare classifier.
   - When a common news/article noun is present, that noun is the head and an `identity-91` (state, author link) links it to the publication.
   - Ability/right/chance noun + verb phrase becomes an `identity-91`; the event gets author `neutral-affirmative`.
   - The "no aspect, no links" rule for apposition `identity-91` now covers only apposition on a named entity.
4. **Compounds.** Any predicate stem (verb or adjective) before 人/者 is split, using `:ARG0-of` or `:ARG1-of` as fits. 全/各/该 + noun becomes `noun :mod 全`. The checklist now says to look up the roleset of every attributive adjective.
5. **Clause-chaining adverbs.** 还, 甚至 and 也 that only mark a clause as additional or climactic within the same sentence get no node.
6. **Concepts and means.**
   - Write `-00` unless `propbank_lookup` returned that exact roleset.
   - A V到 token is one concept.
   - 靠/凭/通过 N gets no node; N is `:reason` of the main verb.
7. **Discourse frames and purpose aspect.** Discourse frames take no aspect and no modal or temporal link. A purpose actually carried out in a past narrative takes the main event's aspect.
8. **Noun-modifier roles.** An issue or matter of X, and a domain noun on a policy-type noun, are `:topic`.
9. **Coordinated conjuncts.** Each later conjunct links to the previous one in a chain, not to the first.
